doc.title: Ametria Dock interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 4, 2019

title: Assessing children brought by parents: pitch matching and honest feedback
summary: Dock assesses pitch and improvisation, prefers parents out of the room, and gives honest feedback, comparing it to her daughter's track coach.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Have you ever had the awkward situation where someone comes to you and maybe you get the feeling they’re coming to you because mom wants them to really. And the young person doesn’t have, is not blessed with a voice.

So most times, for me, when I get a parent that has a child that they feel like they’ve got something, we do an assessment. And so with my kids I generally don’t like for the parents to be in the room because there is so much anxiety when the parent is there. They’re not free to flow. So initially though I let the parents stay in because sometimes I’ve never heard what the child sounds like prior to them coming to me. And so I have the little things that I do just like, so improv exercises as well as checking if they can match pitch and that’s a huge one, because if you have a child that you feel like they have the emotion but they can’t match pitch that’s a huge problem. And most of the time the parent is not a singer so the parent is like just like over the moon with the way that they emote but they don’t understand that we’re not singing in tune.
Right. “What do you mean she can’t match pitches?”

Right. “I don’t understand that.” So I break it down and we talk about it and we have hard conversations sometimes. Because I feel like I’m a mom and I want someone to tell me the truth if my daughter was — my daughter is in track right now and it’s so funny because she’s not really fast. And we laugh because she’s like, “Well it’s good exercise, Mom.” And so like if the coach — my husband is more of a sports — he played college ball and he’s that guy and so he’s like, “No, you can do this.” And I’m like — and she and I are both — she’s such a creative like, “I’m just doing it because I know Dad wants me to do some type of sports.” But the coach is going to give us some feedback and was giving us feedback. And I want whoever’s coaching to be honest you know. Maybe she’ll be better. So yeah, I want to give the same to my clients.
